newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump on falling oil prices, economic data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump on falling oil prices, economic data.

text.p: Stocks posted solid gains Thursday as a sharp drop in oil prices and the latest economic reports boosted bonds and sent long-term interest rates to the lowest levels in nearly 7 months.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 36.15 points at 6,029.38. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,462 to 929 on heavy volume of 482 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond gained more than three-quarters of a point and its yield fell to 6.64 percent -- its lowest level since April 3 -- from 6.71 percent on Wednesday.
"The numbers that came out made the bond market happy," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
"With the GDP numbers yesterday on the soft side, and the unemployment claims today, the feeling is that the economy is soft, and the Fed won't do anything about interest rates," Canelo said.
The Labour Department said initial jobless benefit claims jumped to 342,000 in the week ended Oct. 26 compared with a revised 319,000 in the previous week.
In another report, consumer spending on goods and services rose a scant 0.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.18 trillion in September, after a 0.5 percent gain in August.

This followed news Wednesday that economic growth slowed to a 2.2 percent rate in the third quarter, from a 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter because consumer spending slowed to a near standstill.

Meanwhile, crude oil prices plunged 93 cents to $23.35 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange after rival Kurdish factions agreed to extend a U.S. brokered ceasefire that ended two months of clashes in northern Iraq.
Traders said the news rekindled hopes for the implementation of an Iraqi oil-for-food deal that should add more oil to the world market.
The fall in energy prices also triggered a steep retreat in the Commodity Research Bureau index -- an inflation barometer. The CRB tumbled 3.83 to 237.83.
"The CRB energy numbers are what everybody was talking about," said Frank Calta at Anvil Institutional Services.
"Some key commodity prices are much softer, and that triggered a big bond rally," he said.
Analysts said traders were happy at what they view as the increasing unlikelihood that Democrats would take control of Congress in next Tuesday's elections.
"If the Democrats take over the House, that's bad news for bonds," said Canelo.

Among active issues, Campbell Soup shed 3 to 80 after the company said the grandson of the company founder sold about 9 million shares. In recent months, John Dorrance III has been selling huge blocks of Campbell stock, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The shares of big oil companies fell as crude oil sank. Among losers, Royal Dutch Petroleum dropped 3-3/8 to 165-3/8, Shell Transport skidded 2-3/8 to 98, and Texaco lost 1-3/8 to 101-5/8.

The fall in the price of oil helped airline stocks, including American Airlines' parent AMR Corp., which was up 3-1/8 to 84, United Airlines' parent UAL Corp., up 1-7/8 to 47-3/8, and Delta up 2-1/8 to 70-7/8.
Computer stocks were broadly higher, rebounding from recent declines. International Business Machines rose 2-5/8 to 129, Dell Computer jumped 2-7/16 to 81-3/8, Compaq was up 1-3/4 to 69-5/8.
Swedish-American drug maker Pharmacia & Upjohn lost 1-3/4 to 36 after reporting lower earnings due to currency fluctuations.
Cigna Corp. gained 3-3/8 to 130-1/2 on strong results released Wednesday.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 15.28 points to 1,221.51.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks gained 4.37 to 705.27. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.43 to 568.72.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks gained 1.78 to 374.50. The average share was up 19 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,851.331 up 42.811 or 0.63 percent.
